title: In the Bliss of Old Predicted
description: In the Bliss of Old Predicted in Tonic Solfa to KALMAR, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in 8.7.8.7.7.7, and this page sets them to KALMAR; any other 8.7.8.7.7.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the bliss of old pre-dict-ed, Heaven and earth to day re-joice; Men and an-gels, one in spir-it, Shout a-loud in glee-ful voice; For, to those in dark-ness drear, God in hu-man flesh is near.

lines: In the bliss of old predicted,
Men and angels, one in spirit,
For, to those in darkness drear,
God in human flesh is near.
Cave and manger show the mystery;
Bearing gifts to lay before Him
From the East the Magi hail;
Taught by angel words to sing,
Peace on earth its reign begin!
For the one Desire of nations
Comes to save us from our sin;
From the bondage of the foe.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to KALMAR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
